actions.name: query_data
actions.title: Query data
actions.help: This action allows users to choose data sources and perform query on the data. To get started on using the action, please refer to the video guide here , and our documentation here .

input.name: sources
input.label: Data Sources

properties.name: table_name
properties.label: Data source name
properties.hint: Provide an alias name for the data source. E.g: contacts, orders. This name is to be used in the query.

properties.name: data_source_type
properties.label: Data source type
properties.hint: Provide the data source type. To pass file content directly from upstream action/trigger chooser Content Stream. You can also refer to a file in Workato FileStorage or a table from Data tables.

properties.name: source_stream
properties.label: Content input stream
properties.hint: Pass the contents or file contents reference pill here from an upstream action or trigger.

properties.name: wf_file_path
properties.label: FileStorage file
properties.hint: Provide the FileStorage file full path here to fetch the data. For example, “samplepath/filename.csv”.

properties.name: table_id
properties.label: Data table
properties.hint: Select a data table to fetch the data.

properties.name: file_format
properties.label: File format
properties.hint: Choose the data format.

properties.name: json_jq_expression
properties.label: jq expression
properties.hint: Provide a jq expression to convert your JSON data into CSV format. For example, .items[] | [ keys[] as $k | .[$k] ] | @csv .

properties.name: excel_sheet_name
properties.label: Worksheet
properties.hint: Provide the sheet name from the Excel file where the data is available.

properties.name: excel_range
properties.label: Range
properties.hint: Provide the cell range of the data. e.g A5:F2000. Make sure to include the header row if the schema type selected is ‘Infer’.

properties.name: schema_type
properties.label: Column schema type
properties.hint: Choose ‘Define' to provide column names and types explicitly in the action. Choose ‘Dynamic’ to pass schema as array data pill from upstream action. Choose ‘Infer’ to infer column names and schema aut…

properties.name: table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Describe the column schema of the data in this data source.

properties.name: dynamic_table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Provide the data pill with a schema.

properties.name: excel_table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Describe the schema of the columns of the data source.

properties.name: excel_dynamic_table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Provide the sheet name from the Excel file where the data is available.

properties.name: parquet_table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Describe the schema of the columns of the Parquet data source.

properties.name: parquet_dynamic_table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Provide the data pill with a schema for the Parquet data source.

properties.name: avro_table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Describe the schema of the columns of the Avro data source.

properties.name: avro_dynamic_table_schema
properties.label: Data schema
properties.hint: Provide the data pill with a schema for the Avro data source.

properties.name: allow_relaxed_schema
properties.label: Column relaxation
properties.hint: Select Yes if the incoming source data may contain additional columns than the schema provided. Select No to exactly match schema with the data, and it returns error if additional columns are encounte…

properties.name: csv_ignore_header
properties.label: Contains header
properties.hint: Select Yes if the incoming data contains header as the first row. If so, SQL transformations will understand the columns in the file by name matching the first row in the file with the schema provided…

properties.name: excel_ignore_header
properties.label: Contains header
properties.hint: Set to Yes if the Excel range contain a header row that needs to be ignored. Default is set to No.

properties.name: matching_mode
properties.label: Header matching
properties.hint: Choose how to match header with schema columns

properties.name: csv_delimiter
properties.label: Column delimiter
properties.hint: Select the character that separates columns in the CSV contents. Default is set to comma.

input.hint: Specify data-sources to perform SQL over them

properties.name: parameters
properties.label: Query parameters
properties.hint: Add the parameters to be used in the WHERE condition of the query below. e.g. id. Next, add the actual parameter value, which can be static or datapills. Select the closest corresponding data type tha…

properties.name: sql_select_query
properties.label: SQL query
properties.hint: Add SQL select statement to query one or more data sources. Joins and more complex functions are also supported, more details available here . To add parameters in the WHERE condition, use bind variab…

properties.name: engine
properties.label: Engine
properties.hint: Choose the engine used to execute the query.

properties.name: type
properties.label: Output type
properties.hint: Select the type of the output. Use “Content stream” to share the contents as a streamable data pill to downstream actions. Use FileStorage file option to save output as a file in FileStorage system.

properties.name: wf_file_path
properties.label: FileStorage output folder
properties.hint: Choose or enter the path where the output file needs to be stored in Workato FileStorage. For example, “samplepath/path1/”

properties.name: wf_file_name
properties.label: FileStorage output file name
properties.hint: Define the name of the output file that needs to be stored in Workato FileStorage.

properties.name: mode
properties.label: File action
properties.hint: Choose how the destination file in FileStorage should be handled when the transformation runs. Create fails if the file already exists. Append and Overwrite create the file if it does not exist, or ap…

properties.name: file_format
properties.label: File type
properties.hint: Select the file format of the output data.

properties.name: excel_include_header
properties.label: Include header row
properties.hint: Set to Yes if the column names from the SQL needs to be added as header row in the file. This is useful if file is to be viewed or for generating reports. Default is set to no.

properties.name: excel_sheet_name
properties.label: Sheet name
properties.hint: Set custom sheet name for the Excel file, note that the output data will always be added in the first sheet with this name. Defaults to “Sheet 1“ if no name is provided"

properties.name: excel_start_from
properties.label: Start from
properties.hint: Enter the cell to start inserting the data from. For ex: ‘C1'. Defaults to 'A1’.

properties.name: csv_include_header
properties.label: Include header row
properties.hint: Set to Yes if the column names from the SQL needs to be added as header row in the file. This is useful if file is to be viewed or for generating reports. Default is set to no.

properties.name: csv_delimiter
properties.label: Column delimiter
properties.hint: Select the character that separates columns in the CSV contents. Default is set to comma.

properties.name: csv_quote_style
properties.label: Quote type
properties.hint: Choose whether to use quotation marks around the values in the output. Default is "Use when necessary"

properties.name: csv_quote
properties.label: Quote character
properties.hint: Choose the type of quotation marks to use around the values in the output. Default is "Double"
